description: GIVE EVERY PLAYER THE FULL EIGHT-WAY PASS-TECHNIQUE SET, WITHOUT GIVING HIM THE ACCURACY. This is the exact mechanism the owner described from other games ('some animations only unlock when your passing stat is over 80') - here the number is 70 and the attribute is Low/Short Pass. WHAT THE STOCK CODE DOES, read instruction by instruction at 0x143ffa9db (inside the 4-caller function 0x143ffa950, reached from the kick tree): 'test sil,sil / je 0x143ffaa1d' then 'mov edx,0x1c / call ATTR_get 0x143ea8cb0 / cmp eax,0x46 / jge 0x143ffaa1d', then a second read of the same attribute through 0x1442dd5b0(env, pitch slot, 0x1c) with 'cmp al,0x46 / jae 0x143ffaa1d'. If EITHER read is at least 70 the code lands at 0x143ffaa1d, where the move id at [rbx+0x1c] is checked against 1..8 and dispatched through a jump table. If BOTH reads are below 70 it falls through to 0x143ffaa0f, where the same move id is checked against 1..2 only and anything else bails to 0x143ffae34. So a sub-70 passer is confined to two of the eight techniques at this site. WHAT CHANGES: one inline immediate, 0x143ffa9ed 'cmp eax,0x46' -> 'cmp eax,0x00'. ATTR_get ends in 'movzx eax,al' (0x143ea8cca), so its result is always 0..255 and never negative; 'jge' after 'cmp eax,0' is therefore ALWAYS taken and every player reaches the eight-way dispatch. The second read is then skipped entirely. Instruction length unchanged, no branch touched, no shared pool cell touched. WHY THIS IS THE RIGHT SHAPE FOR THE GOAL: it unlocks the technique WITHOUT raising anybody's Low Pass attribute, so the same attribute still feeds the error model at full strength - vocabulary from the situation, error from ability, exactly as asked. Raising the attribute in the player DATA instead would open the same gate but would also buy the player a better accuracy factor f; that is the honest limit of the data route here and the reason this one belongs in the exe. WHO IT AFFECTS: everyone - the read is of the kicker's own attribute, with no team and no human/CPU branch, so your AI team-mates and the CPU's players get the wider set too. EVIDENCE: b-disassembly (the compare, both branch targets, the 1..2 versus 1..8 range checks and the jump table at 0x143ffaa2b were all read directly); the always-non-negative property of ATTR_get is b-disassembly as well. NOT emulated - I did not drive this function with a controlled world, and I did NOT trace which animation each of move ids 3..8 actually plays. So: 'a sub-70 passer is restricted to 2 of 8 here' is solid; 'those other 6 look like X on screen' is not established. SIDE EFFECTS: low-passing players will now attempt pass techniques they could never attempt before, in situations where the game picks them - if one of ids 3..8 is a showy technique, a limited midfielder will now try it. The error model is untouched, so he will execute it with his own accuracy, which is the intent. No interaction with the card packs (different function, different bytes). WHAT TO LOOK FOR IN ONE MATCH: play a side with a clearly sub-70 short passer (a defensive midfielder or a centre-half in the 60s) and watch his distribution in tight areas - side-foot, outside-of-the-boot, scooped and cushioned balls that he never played before. Then confirm the balls still go astray at his usual rate; if his passing suddenly becomes accurate as well as varied, something else is wrong and you should revert. Bytes at 0x143ffa9ed verified identical in the PRISTINE backup and the installed image; a whole-image scan found no relative branch landing inside 0x143ffa9ee..0x143ffa9ef. REVERT: python tools/exe_patch.py remove tools/data/patches/anime-pass-technique-open.json

patches.name: Low Pass technique gate: cmp eax,0x46 (>=70) -> cmp eax,0x00 (always true, ATTR_get is movzx so never negative)
